whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the CPQ Administrator exam?

personas.label: Administrators supporting an existing CPQ org
personas.description: You maintain a Salesforce CPQ setup built by another team and need to understand its products, rules, pricing, and contract workflows.

personas.label: Revenue operations teams
personas.description: You manage quoting or renewals and want to know which CPQ settings support each part of the sales process.

personas.label: Consultants working with quote-to-cash
personas.description: You know Salesforce and want to build practical knowledge of CPQ objects, configuration rules, and pricing behavior.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the CPQ Administrator exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam asks how Salesforce CPQ handles product configuration, pricing, approvals, and contract changes. General Salesforce administration helps, but CPQ has its own records and pricing sequence, so hands-on practice is valuable.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
65% to pass, which is 39 correct answers out of 60.
Know the rule categories: Product rules control product selection; price rules update quote or quote line fields.
Learn the pricing sequence: Be able to place list, special, regular, customer, and net price in order.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice configuring a bundle, adding rules, and testing prices in a CPQ org. Then contract a quote and work through a renewal and an amendment. Aim for at least 75% on practice sets and explain why the chosen configuration fits each requirement.

examFormat.heading: Salesforce CPQ Administrator exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions cover configuration and quoting tasks.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a sales requirement, such as limiting bundle choices, applying tiered discounts, or changing a contract mid-term. Decide which CPQ feature owns that behavior.
bestWayToPass: Practice in a CPQ org: Build a bundle and use the Quote Line Editor so you can observe how settings affect a quote.
Map the pricing waterfall: Learn the order of price stages and where contracted prices, discount schedules, and manual discounts apply.
Separate rule types: Product rules govern selection and validation; price rules write values to quote fields.
Follow the contract lifecycle: Review how a quote becomes an order, contract, subscriptions, renewal, or amendment.

certificationCard.description: Covers configuring Salesforce CPQ end to end: bundles and product options, product and price rules, the pricing waterfall, discount schedules and approvals, quote documents, and the contract lifecycle through renewals and amendments.

blocks.heading: Product Rules and Price Rules
blocks.body: Product rules control what users can select in a bundle or product search. Validation rules report conditions that must be fixed, selection rules add or change options, alert rules show a warning, and filter rules narrow search results. Price rules use conditions and actions to update quote or quote line fields. Evaluation events determine when a price rule runs, such as Before Calculate or After Calculate. When a scenario asks to control product choices, consider a product rule; when it asks to set a field value, consider a price rule.

blocks.heading: Bundles, Features, and Options
blocks.body: A bundle is a parent product with configurable options, which can be grouped into features. Feature minimum and maximum values control how many options a user can select. An option can have its own quantity and pricing behavior; a bundled option contributes to the parent price instead of showing its own separate total. Configuration attributes let a user make a selection that rules can use to control other options. Nested bundles allow an option to contain another configurable group.

blocks.heading: The Pricing Waterfall
blocks.body: CPQ calculates prices in stages: list price, special price, regular price, customer price, and net price. The price book supplies list price. Contracted prices and block pricing can affect special price; quantity adjustments feed into regular price; discount schedules and manual discounts contribute to customer price; partner or distributor discounts can affect net price. A discount schedule can use slab pricing, where each tier applies to units within that tier, or range pricing, where the reached tier applies to the full quantity.

blocks.heading: Discounts, Contracted Prices, and Approvals
blocks.body: Discount schedules apply configured discounts by volume or term. A contracted price stores a negotiated price for a product and account. Sales users may enter manual discounts, subject to configured limits and approvals. Advanced Approvals supports approval chains and features such as smart approvals, which can skip an approver who already approved an equal or greater discount. Identify whether a question concerns calculating a price or routing a quote for approval.

blocks.heading: Contracts, Subscriptions, Renewals, and Amendments
blocks.body: When a quote is ordered and contracted, CPQ can create subscription records with start and end dates. Renewal forecasting and renewal quoting settings control automatic creation of renewal opportunities and quotes. Amendments change a contract during its active term. The amendment quote uses the contract and its subscriptions as the starting point, and CPQ prorates changes over the remaining term. Keep renewals, which start a new term, separate from amendments, which change the current term.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the CPQ Administrator exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify whether the requirement concerns product selection, field values, pricing, approval, or contract timing. Then choose the CPQ feature that owns that behavior.

blocks.heading: Choose a Rule by Its Effect
blocks.body: A rule that controls bundle choices is a product rule. A rule that updates a quote field is a price rule. Know what each product rule type does.

blocks.heading: Follow the Pricing Stages
blocks.body: Memorize list, special, regular, customer, and net price in sequence. Practice identifying where contracted prices, discount schedules, and manual discounts are applied.

blocks.heading: Compare Slab and Range
blocks.body: With slab pricing, each tier rate applies to units inside that tier. With range pricing, the reached tier applies to all units. Work through sample quantities to see the difference.

blocks.heading: Recognize Advanced Approvals
blocks.body: Smart approvals and approval chains are Advanced Approvals features. A resubmitted quote may skip an approver who approved an equal or larger discount already.

blocks.heading: Distinguish Amendments from Renewals
blocks.body: An amendment changes the active contract and prorates the change over the remaining term. A renewal creates the next term from the contract subscriptions.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next credentials for CPQ administrators
nextCertsAfter.intro: Consider a related product, billing, revenue, or platform credential as your responsibilities grow.

sampleQuestions.question: A bundle should make Premium Support unavailable whenever a buyer selects the Basic tier. Which configuration fits?
options: A selection rule that disables Premium Support
A validation rule that blocks the quote after configuration
A price rule that changes the quote line amount
A discount schedule for the Basic tier
sampleQuestions.explanation: Selection rules can enable or disable bundle options based on another choice, which matches this requirement.
whyWrong: A validation rule reports or blocks an invalid configuration rather than disabling the option as the user chooses.
Price rules update field values and do not control whether a product option is available.
Discount schedules set discounts by volume or term, not option availability.

sampleQuestions.question: A special negotiated amount for one account and product should appear on every future quote. What should the admin create?
options: A separate price book for the account
A contracted price
A discount schedule for all accounts
A manual discount on each quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: A contracted price stores the negotiated account and product price so CPQ can apply it to future quotes.
whyWrong: A separate price book is not the CPQ feature for maintaining a contracted product price.
A discount schedule varies by quantity or term rather than by a particular account price.
Manual entry depends on the user and does not apply automatically.

sampleQuestions.question: A schedule applies the tier reached at 100 units to all 100 units. Which schedule method is this?
options: Slab pricing
Term pricing
Range pricing
Block pricing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Range pricing applies the reached tier to the full quantity, so all 100 units use that tier rate.
whyWrong: Slab pricing applies each tier rate only to the units within that tier.
Term pricing varies by subscription length, not quantity tiers.
Block pricing assigns a fixed price to a quantity block rather than applying a reached discount rate to all units.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer wants 20 more licenses four months into a 12-month contract. What should the admin create?
options: A new quote on a separate opportunity
A renewal quote for the next term
An amendment quote from the contract
An edit to the original quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: An amendment quote changes an active contract and can prorate the additional licenses over the remaining term.
whyWrong: A separate quote would not make the change against the active contract.
A renewal quote is for the next contract term, not a mid-term change.
The contracted sale should be changed through an amendment rather than by editing the original quote.

sampleQuestions.question: At which pricing stage do discount schedules contribute their discount?
options: Special price
Customer price
Net price
List price
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discount schedules contribute to the customer price stage of the CPQ pricing waterfall.
whyWrong: Special price is where mechanisms such as contracted prices and block pricing can apply.
Net price follows customer price and can include partner or distributor discounts.
List price comes from the price book before later pricing adjustments.

sampleQuestions.question: A price rule must set a field before CPQ calculates prices. Which evaluation event should it use?
options: On Save
On Initialization
After Calculate
Before Calculate
sampleQuestions.explanation: Before Calculate runs before the pricing calculation, allowing the rule to set the field in time.
whyWrong: On Save is not a CPQ price rule evaluation event for this purpose.
On Initialization runs when the editor initializes, not immediately before a calculation.
After Calculate occurs after the pricing calculation has completed.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales user should see a warning about an unusual configuration but still be allowed to continue. Which product rule type fits?
options: Validation
Selection
Alert
Filter
sampleQuestions.explanation: An alert rule presents a message without blocking the user from continuing.
whyWrong: Validation rules are used to flag conditions that may prevent a quote from proceeding.
Selection rules change which options are selected or available.
Filter rules limit the products displayed in product search.

sampleQuestions.question: What does CPQ create for subscription products when an ordered quote is contracted?
options: Dated subscription records
Records held until the renewal date
Deleted quote lines
One-time product records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Contracting creates subscription records that represent the service term and support later renewals or amendments.
whyWrong: The subscriptions are created during contracting rather than waiting until renewal.
The quote remains as the record of what was sold; its lines are not simply deleted.
A subscription product remains a subscription rather than becoming a one-time product.

sampleQuestions.question: An approver approved a 20% discount. On resubmission at 15%, the same approver should be skipped. Which feature supports this?
options: A validation rule attached to the quote record
A standard Salesforce approval process
An alert rule shown during product configuration
Smart approvals
sampleQuestions.explanation: Smart approvals can skip an approver who previously approved an equal or greater discount.
whyWrong: Validation rules address record conditions and do not determine whether an approver is repeated.
The requirement describes smart approval behavior rather than a basic approval process.
Product alert rules display messages during configuration and do not route approvals.

sampleQuestions.question: A bundle feature must require at least one and no more than three options. Where should this be set?
options: The option quantity value on each individual product option
The price book entry linked to the parent bundle product
A validation product rule that runs after selections are made
Feature min/max option limits
sampleQuestions.explanation: Feature minimum and maximum values directly set how many options a user must or may select.
whyWrong: Option quantity controls how many units of an option are added, not the number of choices in a feature.
Price book entries define price information rather than selection limits.
A validation rule could report an invalid count, but the feature fields define the selection limits.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the bundled flag on a product option mean for its price?
options: Included in the price of the parent product
The option must always be free
The admin must manually discount it to zero
It always has a separately priced quote line
sampleQuestions.explanation: A bundled option contributes to the parent product price rather than adding a separate option price.
whyWrong: Bundled describes how the price is represented; it does not mean the option has no value.
The bundled setting handles the pricing relationship without a manual zero discount.
A separately priced option is the behavior of an unbundled option.

sampleQuestions.question: Why add a configuration attribute at the top of a bundle configurator?
options: To remove the need for product rules
To store the final quote total
A choice that drives dependent options
To set the contract end date
sampleQuestions.explanation: A configuration attribute lets a user make a choice that selection rules can apply to options below it.
whyWrong: Attributes can provide inputs to product rules rather than replace the rules.
The quote calculation determines totals; a configuration attribute is not the total field.
Contract dates are set through the contract and subscription process.

sampleQuestions.question: A renewal opportunity and quote should be created as a contract approaches its end date. What controls this?
options: The amendment process
Renewal forecast and quote creation settings
A custom scheduled Apex job
A price rule with an After Calculate event
sampleQuestions.explanation: The contract renewal forecasting and renewal quoting settings govern automatic renewal record creation.
whyWrong: Amendments handle changes during the current contract term.
Standard CPQ renewal settings can support this without a custom scheduled job.
Price rules update quote values and do not create renewal opportunities.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a user-entered manual discount not affect the net price as expected?
options: The net price stage does not include discounts entered on a quote
An earlier price stage may set the value before later adjustments
CPQ does not support manual discounts on quoted products
Manual discounts apply only to subscription product lines
sampleQuestions.explanation: The pricing waterfall runs in order, and earlier values or settings can affect how later discounting is calculated.
whyWrong: Net price is calculated after discounts rather than excluding them all.
Manual discounts are a supported CPQ capability.
Discounts can apply to one-time products as well as subscriptions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a product filter rule do?
options: Limits the products returned by search
Writes a value into a target quote field
Blocks a quote from being saved
Calculates prorated charges for an amendment
sampleQuestions.explanation: A filter rule narrows the products returned during product selection based on its conditions.
whyWrong: Writing field values is handled by price rule actions.
A validation rule is used to flag or prevent an invalid quote condition.
Amendment proration is part of CPQ contract change calculations.
